concerns: The comparison baseline is trained with ground-truth cross-entropy only, while SWAM receives hard-label knowledge distillation and a teacher-initialized classification head, so the small reported accuracy margins cannot be attributed to the merging mechanism itself [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].

Reported accuracy differences are very small (mean deltas from +0.02 to +0.26 percentage points, with some negative values) and are based on only one to three seeds, providing weak statistical support for the claimed gains [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].

The aggressive-schedule results show losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, and the abstract's claim of matching or exceeding baseline is qualified by minimal losses, leaving the headline benefit dataset-dependent and not clearly established [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0002, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the methodological concept is clearly presented, the empirical evaluation contains critical confounding factors: SWAM was trained with knowledge distillation and teacher-initialized weights while the comparison baseline was not [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037]. With performance margins being very small (often under 0.2%), this training mismatch introduces substantial uncertainty regarding the actual efficacy of the merging algorithm.

blocking_reasons: The comparison baseline is trained with ground-truth cross-entropy only, while SWAM receives hard-label knowledge distillation and a teacher-initialized classification head, so the small reported accuracy margins cannot be attributed to the merging mechanism itself [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].

Reported accuracy differences are very small (mean deltas from +0.02 to +0.26 percentage points, with some negative values) and are based on only one to three seeds, providing weak statistical support for the claimed gains [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].

The aggressive-schedule results show losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet, and the abstract's claim of matching or exceeding baseline is qualified by minimal losses, leaving the headline benefit dataset-dependent and not clearly established [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0002, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final performance is measured with standard ground-truth classification accuracy and hardware efficiency metrics rather than the saliency or distillation losses used in training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 classification accuracy on held-out test and validation splits, plus FLOPs, throughput, latency, and memory measurements [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0035].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Composite loss combining ground-truth cross-entropy, hard-label knowledge distillation, and KL divergence against block-4 attention rollout [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0021].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Because the full-token baseline does not receive the same knowledge distillation or pre-initialized classification weights during fine-tuning, the reported modest accuracy margins (+0.02% to +0.26%) cannot be cleanly attributed to the SWAM merging mechanism rather than distillation and initialization advantages [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0025, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0037].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Empirical evaluation tests DeiT-Small on CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100 across 1 to 3 seeds, measuring top-1 accuracy, latency, and FLOPs [Ef61cc48d32462636-B0030, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0032, Ef61cc48d32462636-B0035].
